text: All this, whatsoever exists in the universe, should be covered by the Lord. Having renounced (the unreal), enjoy (the Real). Do not covet the wealth of any man.
note: Envy and wanting what others have

tags.when_helps: Someone caught up in wanting what others have, seeking a spiritual way to hold possessions lightly.

display_text: All this, whatsoever exists in the universe, should be covered by the Lord. Having renounced (the unreal), enjoy (the Real). Do not covet the wealth of any man.
plain: Everything that exists in the universe should be seen as pervaded by the Lord. Let go of the unreal and enjoy the Real. Do not covet anyone's wealth.
core_idea: See the Lord in all; covet nothing.

text: He who sees all beings in the Self and the Self in all beings, he never turns away from It (the Self). He who perceives all beings as the Self for him how can there be delusion or grief, when he sees this oneness (everywhere)?
note: Grief and separateness; seeing oneness with all

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling separate and grieving, drawn to the idea that all beings share one Self.

display_text: He who sees all beings in the Self and the Self in all beings, he never turns away from It (the Self). He who perceives all beings as the Self for him how can there be delusion or grief, when he sees this oneness (everywhere)?
plain: Whoever sees all beings in the Self and the Self in all beings never turns away from it. For one who sees all beings as the Self, seeing this oneness everywhere, how can there be delusion or grief?
core_idea: Seeing oneness in all ends delusion and grief.

text: Look back to those who lived before and look to those who live now. Like grain the mortal decays and like grain again springs up (is reborn).
note: Mortality and the cycle of life

tags.when_helps: Someone confronting mortality who may find steadiness in the old cycle of decay and renewal.

display_text: Look back to those who lived before and look to those who live now. Like grain the mortal decays and like grain again springs up (is reborn).
plain: Look at those who lived before and those living now: mortals decay like grain and, like grain, spring up again in rebirth.
core_idea: Mortals die and are reborn like grain.

text: Nachiketas said: O Death, these are fleeting; they weaken the vigour of all the senses in man. Even the longest life is short. Keep thou thy chariots, dance and music. Man cannot be satisfied by wealth.
note: Chasing wealth and pleasure; life is short

tags.when_helps: Someone who has pleasures and wealth yet feels unsatisfied, sensing they are fleeting.

display_text: Nachiketas said: O Death, these are fleeting; they weaken the vigour of all the senses in man. Even the longest life is short. Keep thou thy chariots, dance and music. Man cannot be satisfied by wealth.
plain: Nachiketas tells Death that these pleasures are fleeting and wear out the senses; even the longest life is short. Death can keep his chariots, dancing and music, for wealth never satisfies anyone.

text: Yama said: The good is one thing and the pleasant another. These two, having different ends, bind a man. It is well with him who chooses the good. He who chooses the pleasant misses the true end. The good and the pleasant approach man; the wise examines both and discriminates between them; the wise prefers the good to the pleasant, but the foolish man chooses the pleasant through love of bodily pleasure.
note: Hard choices: what is good versus what is easy

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone torn between what feels pleasant now and what they know is good.

display_text: Yama said: The good is one thing and the pleasant another. These two, having different ends, bind a man. It is well with him who chooses the good. He who chooses the pleasant misses the true end. The good and the pleasant approach man; the wise examines both and discriminates between them; the wise prefers the good to the pleasant, but the foolish man chooses the pleasant through love of bodily pleasure.
plain: Yama says the good and the pleasant differ and lead to different ends. All is well for whoever chooses the good; whoever chooses the pleasant misses the true goal. The wise prefer the good; fools choose pleasure.
core_idea: Choose the good over the merely pleasant.

text: Fools dwelling in ignorance, yet imagining themselves wise and learned, go round and round in crooked ways, like the blind led by the blind.

tags.when_helps: Someone suspecting they or those guiding them are more confident than wise.

display_text: Fools dwelling in ignorance, yet imagining themselves wise and learned, go round and round in crooked ways, like the blind led by the blind.
plain: Fools living in ignorance, yet thinking themselves wise and learned, wander round and round on crooked paths, like the blind led by the blind.
core_idea: The ignorant who think themselves wise go astray.

text: This Self is never born, nor does It die. It did not spring from anything, nor did anything spring from It. This Ancient One is unborn, eternal, everlasting. It is not slain even though the body is slain. If the slayer thinks that he slays, or if the slain thinks that he is slain, both of these know not. For It neither slays nor is It slain.
note: Fear of death; the deathless self

tags.when_helps: Someone afraid of death or grieving a loss, drawn to the idea of a deathless Self.

display_text: This Self is never born, nor does It die. It did not spring from anything, nor did anything spring from It. This Ancient One is unborn, eternal, everlasting. It is not slain even though the body is slain. If the slayer thinks that he slays, or if the slain thinks that he is slain, both of these know not. For It neither slays nor is It slain.
plain: The Self is never born and never dies; it came from nothing and nothing came from it. Unborn and eternal, it is not killed when the body is killed. Whoever thinks they kill or are killed does not understand.
core_idea: The Self is unborn, undying and cannot be slain.

text: The Self is subtler than the subtle, greater than the great; It dwells in the heart of each living being. He who is free from desire and free from grief, with mind and senses tranquil, beholds the glory of the Atman.
note: Inner stillness; freedom from craving and grief

tags.when_helps: Someone seeking stillness beneath desire and grief, interested in the Self within.

display_text: The Self is subtler than the subtle, greater than the great; It dwells in the heart of each living being. He who is free from desire and free from grief, with mind and senses tranquil, beholds the glory of the Atman.
plain: The Self is finer than the finest and greater than the greatest, living in the heart of every being. Whoever is free from desire and grief, with a calm mind and senses, sees the glory of the Atman.
core_idea: A calm, desireless mind sees the Self within.

text: Know the Atman (Self) as the lord of the chariot, and the body as the chariot. Know also the intellect to be the driver and mind the reins. The senses are called the horses; the sense objects are the roads; when the Atman is united with body, senses and mind, then the wise call Him the enjoyer. He who is without discrimination and whose mind is always uncontrolled, his senses are unmanageable, like the vicious horses of a driver. But he who is full of discrimination and whose mind is always controlled, his senses are manageable, like the good horses of a driver.
note: Self-control; impulses pulling you off course

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone whose senses and impulses keep running away with them, wanting to take the reins.

display_text: Know the Atman (Self) as the lord of the chariot, and the body as the chariot. Know also the intellect to be the driver and mind the reins. The senses are called the horses; the sense objects are the roads; when the Atman is united with body, senses and mind, then the wise call Him the enjoyer. He who is without discrimination and whose mind is always uncontrolled, his senses are unmanageable, like the vicious horses of a driver. But he who is full of discrimination and whose mind is always controlled, his senses are manageable, like the good horses of a driver.
plain: The Atman is the chariot's owner, the body the chariot, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins, the senses the horses. Without discernment and a controlled mind the senses run wild; with them, they obey like good horses.
core_idea: A disciplined mind steers the senses well.

plain_judge.issue: Drops the Atman as enjoyer when united with body, senses and mind.

text: Arise! Awake! Having reached the Great Ones (illumined Teachers), gain understanding. The path is as sharp as a razor, impassable and difficult to travel, so the wise declare.
note: Waking up to a hard path; seeking guidance

tags.when_helps: A seeker finding the path hard, needing a call to wake up and seek good teachers.

display_text: Arise! Awake! Having reached the Great Ones (illumined Teachers), gain understanding. The path is as sharp as a razor, impassable and difficult to travel, so the wise declare.
plain: Arise, awake! Seek out the great teachers and gain understanding. The wise say the path is as sharp as a razor's edge, hard to cross and hard to travel.
core_idea: Wake up; the path is hard but walk it.

text: The Self-existent created the senses out-going; for this reason man sees the external, but not the inner Atman (Self). Some wise man, however, desiring immortality, with eyes turned away (from the external) sees the Atman within. Children (the ignorant) pursue external pleasures; (thus) they fall into the wide- spread snare of death. But the wise, knowing the nature of immortality, do not seek the permanent among fleeting things.
note: Looking outward for fulfilment; turning inward

tags.when_helps: Someone chasing outer pleasures who senses lasting good must be sought within.

display_text: The Self-existent created the senses out-going; for this reason man sees the external, but not the inner Atman (Self). Some wise man, however, desiring immortality, with eyes turned away (from the external) sees the Atman within. Children (the ignorant) pursue external pleasures; (thus) they fall into the wide-spread snare of death. But the wise, knowing the nature of immortality, do not seek the permanent among fleeting things.
display_fix: Word broken by hyphen and space
plain: The senses face outward, so we see the outer world, not the inner Atman. A wise person seeking immortality turns inward and sees the Self. The ignorant chase pleasures into death's snare; the wise seek nothing lasting in fleeting things.
core_idea: Turn inward to find the lasting Self.

plain_judge.issue: Drops the Self-existent as the one who made the senses outgoing.

text: As the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not defiled by external impurities seen by the eyes, thus the one inner Self of all living beings is not defiled by the misery of the world, being outside it.
note: Feeling tainted by suffering; an untouched inner self

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling stained by the misery around them, drawn to an inner self untouched by it.

display_text: As the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not defiled by external impurities seen by the eyes, thus the one inner Self of all living beings is not defiled by the misery of the world, being outside it.
plain: Just as the sun, the eye of the world, is not stained by the impurities it lights up, the one inner Self of all beings is not stained by the world's misery, being beyond it.
core_idea: The inner Self is untouched by the world's misery.

text: When the five organs of perception become still, together with the mind, and the intellect ceases to be active: that is called the highest state. This firm holding back of the senses is what is known as Yoga. Then one should become watchful, for Yoga comes and goes.
note: Meditation; stillness that comes and goes

tags.when_helps: A meditator learning to still the senses and mind, and to stay watchful when stillness slips.

display_text: When the five organs of perception become still, together with the mind, and the intellect ceases to be active: that is called the highest state. This firm holding back of the senses is what is known as Yoga. Then one should become watchful, for Yoga comes and goes.
plain: When the five senses and the mind fall still and the intellect stops working, that is the highest state. This steady restraint of the senses is Yoga. Then stay watchful, because Yoga comes and goes.
core_idea: Stilling the senses is Yoga; stay watchful.

text: When all desires dwelling in the heart cease, then the mortal becomes immortal and attains Brahman here. When all the ties of the heart are cut asunder here, then the mortal becomes immortal. Such is the teaching.
note: Letting go of craving and attachment

tags.when_helps: A seeker longing for freedom from the pull of desire.

display_text: When all desires dwelling in the heart cease, then the mortal becomes immortal and attains Brahman here. When all the ties of the heart are cut asunder here, then the mortal becomes immortal. Such is the teaching.
plain: When all the desires in the heart fall away, the mortal becomes immortal and reaches Brahman here and now. When all the heart's knots are cut, the mortal becomes immortal. That is the teaching.

text: He who thinks he knows It not, knows It. He who thinks he knows It, knows It not. The true knowers think they can never know It (because of Its infinitude), while the ignorant think they know It.
note: Humility before what cannot be fully known

tags.when_helps: Someone frustrated they cannot grasp the divine, or too sure they already have.

display_text: He who thinks he knows It not, knows It. He who thinks he knows It, knows It not. The true knowers think they can never know It (because of Its infinitude), while the ignorant think they know It.
plain: Whoever thinks they do not know Brahman knows it; whoever thinks they know it does not. True knowers feel they can never know it, being infinite, while the ignorant think they do.
core_idea: Those who know the Infinite admit they cannot know it.
